title: Bizarre dog stabbing leaves Chilliwack man dead and RCMP under investigation for Taser use
subtitle: A man alleged to have been stabbing a dog on Wednesday afternoon died following a struggle with police. The dog has been taken to a veterinarian for treatment
article: An investigation will be launched after a man alleged to have been stabbing a dog died following a struggle with police.
At about 4:11 p.m. Wednesday, Chilliwack RCMP responded to a call about a man stabbing a dog.
Upon arrival, police found the suspect inside a residence, where he allegedly struggled during the arrest.
Officers then used a Taser on the suspect. The suspect became "unresponsive" and was sent to hospital before later being pronounced dead.
One police officer was also injured during the incident, but has since been treated and released. The dog was also taken to a veterinarian for treatment.
No further details about the suspect or the condition of the injured officer or dog were released.
Because the suspect was in police custody when he died, the matter will now be probed by the Independent Investigations Office of B.C.
"Given that this matter is now considered a police in-custody death, the IIO BC has asserted jurisdiction and is now on scene," said Insp. Ed Boettcher in a statement released late Wednesday.
Ralph Krenz, a spokesman for the Independent Investigations Office, said a team of five investigators including a forensic specialist had been sent to the scene.
Krenz said they'll be collecting evidence, speaking to witnesses, looking for surveillance video that may exist and interviewing the police officers.
The deceased man's identity has not yet been released.

The man's death comes as Crown prosecutors prepare their case against an officer they allege lied to investigators and perjured himself in relation to the 2007 death of Polish immigrant Robert Dziekanski at Vancouver International Airport. Dziekanski was Tasered by the officer then died.
